title: Executed and imagined grasp forces recorded with stereo-EEG (Murphy et al., 2016): 4 participants, power and pinch force-matching
description: Stereo-EEG recordings from four adults with drug-resistant epilepsy performing force-matching tasks with a power grasp and a lateral pinch. Two participants also completed blocks in which they only imagined producing the force. Each block contained trials at three force targets (20, 30 and 40% of maximum voluntary contraction). The data are intended for studying how subsurface cortical modulations, including those in motor and insular cortex, discriminate executed and imagined grasp forces.
methods_description: Stereo-EEG was recorded at 2000 Hz with a Neuroport amplifier from depth electrodes, alongside an analog dynamometer force signal. Participants matched force targets shown for 5 s, followed by 5 s of rest. Original Blackrock NSx files were converted losslessly to BrainVision format, and target periods from the Simulink log were written to events.tsv.
